1.1.1.name: Non-text Content
1.1.1.plain: Images, icons and controls have a text alternative.

1.2.1.name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
1.2.1.plain: Recorded audio or video has a text alternative.

1.2.3.name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
1.2.3.plain: Recorded video has an audio description or a text alternative.

1.2.5.name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
1.2.5.plain: Recorded video has an audio description.

1.2.6.name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
1.2.6.plain: Recorded audio has sign language interpretation.

1.2.7.name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
1.2.7.plain: Video pauses where needed to fit a full audio description.

1.2.8.name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
1.2.8.plain: Recorded video has a full text alternative.

1.2.9.name: Audio-only (Live)
1.2.9.plain: Live audio has a text alternative.

1.3.1.name: Info and Relationships
1.3.1.plain: Headings, lists, tables and labels are marked up, so assistive technology conveys the same structure people see.

1.3.2.name: Meaningful Sequence
1.3.2.plain: Content is read out in an order that makes sense.

1.3.3.name: Sensory Characteristics
1.3.3.plain: Instructions do not rely only on shape, size, position or sound.

1.3.4.name: Orientation
1.3.4.plain: Works in both portrait and landscape.

1.3.5.name: Identify Input Purpose
1.3.5.plain: Form fields about the user say what they are for, so browsers can fill them in.

1.3.6.name: Identify Purpose
1.3.6.plain: The purpose of regions, controls and icons can be read by software.

1.4.1.name: Use of Color
1.4.1.plain: Colour is never the only way information is shown.

1.4.2.name: Audio Control
1.4.2.plain: Sound that plays by itself can be paused or turned down.

1.4.3.name: Contrast (Minimum)
1.4.3.plain: Text stands out clearly from its background.

1.4.4.name: Resize Text
1.4.4.plain: Text can be enlarged to twice its size without losing anything.

1.4.5.name: Images of Text
1.4.5.plain: Text is real text, not a picture of text.

1.4.6.name: Contrast (Enhanced)
1.4.6.plain: Text has a higher contrast with its background.

1.4.7.name: Low or No Background Audio
1.4.7.plain: Speech is not drowned out by background sound.

1.4.8.name: Visual Presentation
1.4.8.plain: Blocks of text can be shown in the colours, width and spacing a reader needs.

1.4.9.name: Images of Text (No Exception)
1.4.9.plain: Pictures of text are used only for decoration or logos.

1.4.10.name: Reflow
1.4.10.plain: Works on a phone-width screen, or zoomed to 400%, without scrolling sideways.

1.4.11.name: Non-text Contrast
1.4.11.plain: Controls, icons and focus rings stand out from what is around them.

1.4.12.name: Text Spacing
1.4.12.plain: Nothing is lost when a reader widens the spacing between lines, words and letters.

1.4.13.name: Content on Hover or Focus
1.4.13.plain: Pop-ups that appear on hover or focus can be dismissed, and stay while they are being read.

2.1.1.name: Keyboard
2.1.1.plain: Everything can be done with a keyboard alone.

2.1.3.name: Keyboard (No Exception)
2.1.3.plain: Everything can be done with a keyboard, with no exceptions.

2.1.4.name: Character Key Shortcuts
2.1.4.plain: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off or changed.

2.2.1.name: Timing Adjustable
2.2.1.plain: Time limits can be turned off, adjusted or extended.

2.2.2.name: Pause, Stop, Hide
2.2.2.plain: Moving or updating content can be paused or hidden.

2.2.3.name: No Timing
2.2.3.plain: No task has a time limit.

2.2.4.name: Interruptions
2.2.4.plain: Interruptions can be postponed or turned off.

2.2.5.name: Re-authenticating
2.2.5.plain: Signing in again after a session ends loses no work.

2.2.6.name: Timeouts
2.2.6.plain: Users are warned how long inactivity can last before work is lost.

2.3.1.name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
2.3.1.plain: Nothing flashes more than three times a second.

2.3.2.name: Three Flashes
2.3.2.plain: Nothing flashes more than three times a second, at any size.

2.3.3.name: Animation from Interactions
2.3.3.plain: Motion caused by interaction can be turned off.

2.4.1.name: Bypass Blocks
2.4.1.plain: There is a way to skip past navigation repeated on every page.

2.4.2.name: Page Titled
2.4.2.plain: Every page has a title that says what it is.

2.4.3.name: Focus Order
2.4.3.plain: The keyboard moves through the page in a sensible order.

2.4.4.name: Link Purpose (In Context)
2.4.4.plain: Each link says where it goes, together with the text around it.

2.4.5.name: Multiple Ways
2.4.5.plain: There is more than one way to find a page.

2.4.6.name: Headings and Labels
2.4.6.plain: Headings and labels describe what they introduce.

2.4.7.name: Focus Visible
2.4.7.plain: You can always see which control the keyboard is on.

2.4.8.name: Location
2.4.8.plain: You can tell where you are within the application.

2.4.9.name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
2.4.9.plain: Each link's own text says where it goes.

2.4.11.name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
2.4.11.plain: The control the keyboard is on is never completely hidden behind something else.

2.4.12.name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
2.4.12.plain: No part of the control the keyboard is on is hidden behind something else.

2.4.13.name: Focus Appearance
2.4.13.plain: The focus indicator is large and clear enough to see easily.

2.5.1.name: Pointer Gestures
2.5.1.plain: Anything done with a multi-finger or path gesture can also be done with a single tap or click.

2.5.2.name: Pointer Cancellation
2.5.2.plain: A click or tap can be cancelled by moving away before letting go.

2.5.3.name: Label in Name
2.5.3.plain: A control's spoken name includes the words shown on it.

2.5.4.name: Motion Actuation
2.5.4.plain: Nothing needs the device to be shaken or tilted.

2.5.5.name: Target Size (Enhanced)
2.5.5.plain: Controls are at least 44 by 44 pixels.

2.5.6.name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
2.5.6.plain: Any input method can be used, and switched between.

2.5.7.name: Dragging Movements
2.5.7.plain: Anything done by dragging can also be done without dragging.

2.5.8.name: Target Size (Minimum)
2.5.8.plain: Controls are big enough, or far enough apart, to press easily.

3.1.1.name: Language of Page
3.1.1.plain: Each page states its language, so it is read out correctly.

3.1.2.name: Language of Parts
3.1.2.plain: Text in another language is marked as such.

3.1.3.name: Unusual Words
3.1.3.plain: Unusual words and jargon are explained.

3.1.5.name: Reading Level
3.1.5.plain: Text is easy to read, or has a simpler version.

3.1.6.name: Pronunciation
3.1.6.plain: Words whose meaning depends on pronunciation are explained.

3.2.1.name: On Focus
3.2.1.plain: Moving the keyboard onto a control never changes the page by itself.

3.2.2.name: On Input
3.2.2.plain: Changing a setting never changes the page unexpectedly.

3.2.3.name: Consistent Navigation
3.2.3.plain: Navigation appears in the same place and order on every page.

3.2.4.name: Consistent Identification
3.2.4.plain: Things that do the same job are labelled the same way.

3.2.5.name: Change on Request
3.2.5.plain: The page changes only when the user asks it to.

3.2.6.name: Consistent Help
3.2.6.plain: Help appears in the same place on every page that offers it.

3.3.1.name: Error Identification
3.3.1.plain: Mistakes are pointed out in words.

3.3.2.name: Labels or Instructions
3.3.2.plain: Form fields say what to enter.

3.3.3.name: Error Suggestion
3.3.3.plain: Error messages say how to fix the mistake.

3.3.4.name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
3.3.4.plain: Important submissions can be checked, corrected or undone.

3.3.5.name: Help
3.3.5.plain: Help is available where it is needed.

3.3.6.name: Error Prevention (All)
3.3.6.plain: Every submission can be checked, corrected or undone.

3.3.7.name: Redundant Entry
3.3.7.plain: Information already given is not asked for again.

3.3.8.name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
3.3.8.plain: Signing in does not require a memory or puzzle test, and allows password managers and pasting.

3.3.9.name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
3.3.9.plain: Signing in requires no memory or recognition test at all.

4.1.1.name: Parsing (removed in WCAG 2.2)
4.1.1.plain: No longer part of WCAG 2.2; listed only because older tools still report it.

4.1.2.name: Name, Role, Value
4.1.2.plain: Every control tells assistive technology what it is, what it is called and what state it is in.

4.1.3.name: Status Messages
4.1.3.plain: Messages that appear without moving focus are still read out.
